documents.title: Board Meeting Outcome for Outcome Of The Board Meeting

analysis.summary: Amal Ltd reported a 77% increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 240 crore for FY 2025-26, largely driven by a 164% spike in raw material sulphur prices alongside a 3% volume growth. Profit before tax declined by 14% on a consolidated basis as the company was unable to fully absorb higher input costs, leading to reduced EBITDA margins of 16%. The company remains debt-free with an increased cash surplus of Rs 38 crore and recommended a higher dividend of Rs 1.5 per share. Management completed sulphur yard upgradation and is executing three ongoing capex initiatives while evaluating two future growth projects. Amal Ltd reported an improved performance for FY 2024-25, with consolidated sales increasing by 57% to Rs 135 crore and PBT increasing to Rs 33 crore.

guidance.claim: Management has identified three key objectives to strengthen the company further.
guidance.quote: At this time, we have three key objectives to strengthen our Company further:

guidance.claim: The company aims to expand selected existing products and add new related products.
guidance.quote: • Two, to expand (selected existing products) and add new related products.

guidance.claim: The company plans to strengthen its leadership team to secure future growth.
guidance.quote: • Three, to further strengthen the leadership team to secure future growth.

guidance.claim: The company aims to develop a future-fit and purpose-led entity.
guidance.quote: The aim is to develop a future-fit and purpose-led entity.

demand_outlook.claim: Higher price realization and capacity utilization were the main contributors to financial performance.
demand_outlook.quote: The main contributors were higher price realisation and capacity utilisation.

capex_expansion.claim: The company is evaluating two growth projects to expand business operations.
capex_expansion.quote: Our Company is evaluating two growth projects and will decide the next steps while keeping in focus the external business environment.

capex_expansion.claim: Two CapEx proposals totaling Rs 6 crore are underway to upgrade the existing manufacturing facility.
capex_expansion.quote: • One, to invest in upgrading the existing manufacturing facility – two CapEx proposals of ` 6 cr are underway.

capex_expansion.claim: Consolidated capital expenditure for FY 2024-25 was Rs 352 lakh.

margins_costs.claim: The company implemented two projects to improve steam generation and recovery.
margins_costs.quote: The Company implemented two projects for better steam generation and recovery.

margins_costs.claim: The company is exploring measures to optimize resource utilization while maintaining cost efficiency.
margins_costs.quote: The Company is exploring measures to optimise resource utilisation while ensuring cost efficiency.

margins_costs.claim: The price of Sulphur, the primary raw material used by the company, fluctuates on a monthly basis.
margins_costs.quote: The price of the key raw material Sulphur, varies from month to month.

orders_capacity.claim: Higher capacity utilization was a major contributor to performance improvement in FY 2024-25.
orders_capacity.quote: The main contributors were higher price realisation and capacity utilisation.

capital_allocation.claim: The company wiped out its remaining carried forward loss of Rs 14 crore.
capital_allocation.quote: • It wiped out its remaining carried forward loss of ` 14 cr which at peak was ` 56 cr.

capital_allocation.claim: The company repaid all borrowings and accumulated a cash surplus of Rs 22 crore as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: • It repaid its entire borrowing and generated cash surplus of ` 22 cr (as on March 31, 2025).

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a 10% dividend for shareholder approval.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board recommended 10% dividend for your consideration, and we trust you will unanimously approve the same.

capital_allocation.claim: Amal Speciality Chemicals Ltd expanded its paid-up share capital by issuing 50,00,000 preference shares of Rs 10 each to holding company Amal Ltd.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year under review, the Company increased paid-up share capital by way of allotment of 50,00,000 (fifty lakhs) 10.5% non-cumulative redeemable preference shares of ` 10 each to the holding company, Amal Ltd through preferential allotment process at the Board meeting held February 15, 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Key input costs fluctuate monthly due to volatility in Sulphur prices.
risks_headwinds.quote: The price of the key raw material Sulphur, varies from month to month.
